text:
alice_ml: heads-up — after bringing up rwinf-v2-int4 on staging we see a consistent quality regression for CJK->EN pairs, also mixed CJK+latin token splits look different.

alice_ml: quick numbers from the nightly eval: ja->en BLEU drops 29.4 -> 24.1, zh->en BLEU 31.2 -> 26.0, chrF drops ~3.2. token-boundary mismatch rate up +0.8% on mixed-script test set.

carlos_research: ugh. did we change the tokenizer or only the quant kernels?

alice_ml: only quant kernels and a small kernel-selection heuristic tweak in the runtime (prefer fused matmul for seq<128). tokenizer artifacts only visible after quant bringup though.

ben_infra: can you paste a minimal repro? which model variant and config?

alice_ml: model: rwinf-2025-encoder-decoder-v2 (float->int4). config snippet: ```{
  "quant_scheme": "GPTQ-int4-opt",
  "per_channel": true,
  "kv_cache": "enabled",
  "kernel_policy": "fused-prefer"
}```

alice_ml: sample source: "東京都に行ったことがありますか? I love the city vibe."
alice_ml: float output tokens: "東京都 に 行っ た こと が あります か ? I love the city vibe ."
alice_ml: int4 output tokens:  "東 京 都 に 行っ た こと が あります か ? I love the city vibe ."

carlos_research: hmm the int4 split "東京" -> "東 京" — that suggests subword vocab indices are being mapped differently after quant rounding. Could be embedding table alignment or a bad remap in the conversion step.

diane_sre: infra note: we rolled a runtime kernel selection change yesterday at 03:12 UTC (canary -> staging). I can pin staging back to previous runtime if you want a quick A/B.

ben_infra: please post the exact eval command you ran (so I can reproduce locally).

alice_ml: eval harness command: ```./run_eval.py --model rwinf-v2-int4 --split mixed_cjk_test --tokenizer rwinf-vocab-2025 --metrics bleu,chrF,tok-mismatch --batch 64```

alice_ml: attaching a short diff of token ids around the split (float vs int4): ```float_ids:  [..., 54321, 1122, 9087, ...]
int4_ids:   [..., 54321,  256,  1122, 9087, ...]  # extra boundary id 256 inserted```

carlos_research: that extra boundary id 256 reads like a reserved joiner/gap token. Could be an off-by-one during quant table remap. I'll run local bisect across the quant converter commits.

eval-bot: nightly-eval | rwinf-v2-int4 | mixed_cjk_test | ja->en BLEU: 24.1 (-5.3) | zh->en BLEU: 26.0 (-5.2) | tok-mismatch: +0.8%

diane_sre: recording an incident ticket for traceability: INC-2026-089 (will link CPU/GPU kernels and deploy logs).

ben_infra: if it's a converter bug we should be able to reproduce by running the converter with seed X and diffing the produced vocab remap. carlos, when you bisect, check both the quant table and the vocab remapping step.

alice_ml: temporary mitigation: rolling back runtime kernel-policy on staging removed the token split but int4 still slightly lower BLEU (~1.2). so two things: kernel heuristic + converter remap interacting.

carlos_research: noted. I'll start bisect now. expected time ~ 2-3 hrs. ping me if you have more failure examples (especially with ZWJ/zero-width joiners and mixed latin).

alice_ml: adding 3 more examples to the thread I found: 1) "김치가 맛있다, right?" 2) "北京大学(PEKING UNIVERSITY) is..." 3) "e-mail@example.com 你好" — in all int4 we see extra splits around parentheses, emails, and ZWJ+latin.

ben_infra: thanks. I'll hold the staging rollout until bisect finishes. :thumbsup:

alice_ml: thanks all. will post bisect results and a minimal reproducer.
